title: A coarse Menger theorem for hyperbolic graphs, finitely presented groups, and more
summary: Menger's theorem is one of the most fundamental results in graph theory. It states that if a graph $G$ does not contain $k$ disjoint paths between two given sets $X$ and $Y$ of vertices in $G$, then there is a set of at most $k-1$ vertices that intersects every path between $X$ and $Y$. Nguyen, Scott, and Seymour gave a counterexample to the conjectured natural coarse variant in which the paths are required to be pairwise at distance at least $d$, and, conversely, there is a set of at most $k-1$ bounded-radius balls intersecting every path between $X$ and $Y$.
